title: Authorization and Ownership
readerIntent: Understand route, group, permission, schema, field, and record-ownership enforcement.
owner: Each target module owns route and data authorization; identity governance owns principal/group integrity
summary: Authentication evidence never grants universal access; each target operation enforces token class, permission, tenant, schema action, field visibility, ownership, and business policy.

sections.heading: Policy layers
items: User groups compose catalogued permissions through active acyclic inheritance.
Routes enforce required token class, permissions, and API exposure.
Schemas define action/group access, field masking, and ownership policy.
Customer-owned records constrain ownerId; explicit administrative and trusted-service groups may bypass only according to layered policy.
Cross-tenant internal-token access requires a separate permission.

sections.heading: Extension
items: Reusable policy names and mappings belong in properties.js, not closure constants inside schemas.
Projects may add stricter layered policy but must not silently weaken framework security.
Axis discovers allowed contracts and renders controls; backend services remain authoritative.
Nested creation and related-record selection invoke each related schema's permissions and validation.

sections.heading: Verification
items: Field read/write masking and immutable values.
Inactive, missing, cyclic, or inherited groups.
Human, customer, service, scheduled, same-tenant, and cross-tenant boundaries.
